CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSTOREDPROC

CFSTOREDPROC calls a procedure stored in the database itself. Nested CFPROCPARAM tags pass its parameters and receive its output parameters; CFPROCRESULT tags turn the result sets it returns into ordinary query variables. Like an ODBC driver, KoldFusion sends the call as {? = call Name(?, ?)} and binds the parameters by position, or by name when CFPROCPARAM has a DBVARNAME.

The KoldFusion Flat-File Driver keeps each procedure as a text file next to the tables of its data source. Create one with a CREATE PROCEDURE statement in a CFQUERY (see Usage); the cfsnippets data source comes with GetEmployeesByDept, AddEmployee, CountByDept and GetEmployee.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="procedure_name"
    DATASOURCE="ds_name"
    USERNAME="username"
    PASSWORD="password"
    DBSERVER="dbms"
    DBNAME="database_name"
    BLOCKFACTOR="blocksize"
    PROVIDER="COMProvider"
    PROVIDERDSN="datasource"
    DEBUG="Yes/No"
    RETURNCODE="Yes/No">
  CFPROCPARAM and CFPROCRESULT tags
</CFSTOREDPROC>

Attributes

PROCEDURE
Required. Name of the stored procedure. An owner prefix such as dbo.AddEmployee is accepted.
DATASOURCE
Required. Data source that holds the procedure.
USERNAME
Optional. Overrides the login name in the data source definition. The flat-file driver does not check it.
PASSWORD
Optional. Overrides the password in the data source definition. The flat-file driver does not check it.
DBSERVER
Optional. Server name for native drivers. Ignored by the flat-file driver.
DBNAME
Optional. Database name for native drivers. Ignored by the flat-file driver.
BLOCKFACTOR
Optional, default "1". Rows fetched from the server at a time, 1 to 100. Other values are rejected.
PROVIDER
Optional. COM provider for OLE DB data sources.
PROVIDERDSN
Optional. Data source name for the COM provider (OLE DB only).
DEBUG
Optional, default "No". Yes lists the call, every parameter and the number of result sets in the debugging output, even when "Show query information" is off in the Administrator.
RETURNCODE
Optional, default "No". Yes puts the procedure's status code, the value of its RETURN statement, in CFSTOREDPROC.StatusCode.

Usage

After the call, CFSTOREDPROC.ExecutionTime holds the time the procedure took, in milliseconds, and with RETURNCODE="Yes" CFSTOREDPROC.StatusCode holds its status code (0 when the procedure has no RETURN). Errors raised by the procedure arrive as Database exceptions with the usual ODBC SQLState, for example 37000 for an unknown procedure and 07001 for a missing or extra parameter.

Writing procedures

The flat-file driver speaks the procedure dialect of SQL Server and Sybase. A procedure declares its parameters with an @, a type, an optional default and OUTPUT for output parameters:

CREATE PROCEDURE RaiseSalary
    @EmpID   INT,
    @Percent NUMERIC(5,2) = 5,
    @Salary  MONEY OUTPUT
AS
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE Emp_ID = @EmpID)
        RETURN 1;
    UPDATE Employees SET Salary = Salary * (100 + @Percent) / 100 WHERE Emp_ID = @EmpID;
    SELECT @Salary = Salary FROM Employees WHERE Emp_ID = @EmpID;
    RETURN 0;
END

The body can use any SQL the driver understands, with @variables wherever a value may appear, plus:

Statement What it does
DECLARE @v type [, ...] Declares local variables (initially NULL).
SET @v = expression Assigns a value; the expression may be a subquery: SET @n = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Parks).
SELECT @v = column, ... FROM ... Assigns from a query (the last row wins; no rows leaves the variables alone).
SELECT ... Any other SELECT returns a result set to the caller.
IF condition statement [ELSE statement] Conditions may use EXISTS, IN, subqueries and IS NULL.
WHILE condition statement Loops, with BREAK and CONTINUE.
BEGIN ... END Groups statements.
RETURN [n] Ends the procedure with status code n (default 0).
EXEC proc args Calls another procedure: positional, @name = value, DEFAULT and @v OUTPUT arguments, EXEC @rc = proc.
RAISERROR ('text %s', 16, 1, args) Fails with your own message; severity 10 or less is ignored.
PRINT, SET NOCOUNT ON, BEGIN TRAN, COMMIT Accepted and ignored (use CFTRANSACTION for transactions).

@@ROWCOUNT, @@IDENTITY and @@NESTLEVEL work as in SQL Server. Separate statements with semicolons or start each one on a statement keyword. Remove a procedure with DROP PROCEDURE name; change one with ALTER PROCEDURE.

In a CFQUERY you can also call a procedure with EXEC name args, {call name(args)} or CALL name(args); the query receives the procedure's first result set. A CFQUERY may also hold a whole batch that uses variables, for example DECLARE @n INT; SET @n = 5; SELECT TOP @n ....

Note  Procedures, like the tables, live in the data source's directory under kfroot/db/, one .prc file each. The Administrator's table browser (Data Sources > ODBC > View Tables) lists them with their parameters and source.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Department head counts: two result sets, an output parameter and a status code --->
<CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="CountByDept" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" RETURNCODE="Yes">
  <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" DBVARNAME="@Department" NULL="Yes">
  <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="Out" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_INTEGER" DBVARNAME="@Total" VARIABLE="TotalStaff">
  <CFPROCRESULT NAME="HeadCount" RESULTSET="1">
  <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Offices" RESULTSET="2">
</CFSTOREDPROC>

<CFOUTPUT>
<P>CountByDept returned status #CFSTOREDPROC.StatusCode# in #CFSTOREDPROC.ExecutionTime# ms:
#TotalStaff# employees in #HeadCount.RecordCount# departments.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR BGCOLOR="#CCCCCC"><TH>Department</TH><TH>Employees</TH><TH>Payroll</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="HeadCount">
<TR><TD>#Department#</TD><TD ALIGN="right">#Employees#</TD><TD ALIGN="right">#DollarFormat(Payroll)#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
<P>Offices:
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Offices">#Dept_Name# (#Location#)<CFIF CurrentRow LT RecordCount>, </CFIF></CFOUTPUT></P>
